message.content:
{
  "decision": "APPLY",
  "workflow_yaml": "name: Build
on:
  push:
    branches:
      - master
      - branch-*
      - dogfood-*
  pull_request:
  merge_group:
  workflow_dispatch:

concurrency:
  group: >-
    ${{ github.workflow }}-
    ${{ github.event.pull_request.base.ref || 'push' }}-
    ${{ github.event.pull_request.number || github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

env:
  CACHE_BACKEND: s3

jobs:
  build-number:
    outputs:
      BUILD_NUMBER: ${{ steps.build-number.outputs.BUILD_NUMBER }}
    runs-on: sonar-xs
    name: Get build number
    permissions:
      id-token: write
      contents: write
    steps:
      - uses: SonarSource/ci-github-actions/get-build-number@c3a85ac3a2f67f86966e2fb1fdf9a7c1bdc997dc # 2.2.0
        id: build-number

  build:
    runs-on: sonar-xs
    needs: build-number
    name: Build
    permissions:
      id-token: write
      contents: write
    env:
      BUILD_NUMBER: ${{ needs.build-number.outputs.BUILD_NUMBER }}
    outputs:
      build_number: ${{ steps.build.outputs.build_number }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      - uses: jdx/mise-action@9149ea85001c7435d5a66bb127d6a1b6227cb0a5 # v5.0.0
        with:
          version: 2026.10.21
      - uses: SonarSource/ci-github-actions/build-maven@c3a85ac3a2f67f86966e2fb1fdf9a7c1bdc997dc # 2.2.0
        id: build
        with:
          sonar-platform: none
          deploy-pull-request: true
          artifactory-reader-role: private-reader
          artifactory-deployer-role: qa-deployer
          repox-url: https://repox-internal.dev.sonar.build
          maven-args: -T 1C -P dist-no-arch,dist-windows_x64,dist-linux_x64,dist-linux_aarch64,dist-macosx_x64,dist-macosx_aarch64 -Dmaven.test.skip=true -Dsonar.skip=true
      - name: Config Maven (cache setup)
        run: |
          mvn -B -e -V -Pits dependency:go-offline # populate cache including ITs deps too

  test-linux:
    needs: [ build-number, build ]
    runs-on: sonar-m
    name: Test (Linux, Sonar Next)
    permissions:
      id-token: write
      contents: write
    env:
      BUILD_NUMBER: ${{ needs.build-number.outputs.BUILD_NUMBER }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0
      - uses: jdx/mise-action@9149ea85001c7435d5a66bb127d6a1b6227cb0a5 # v5.0.0
        with:
          version: 2026.10.21
      - name: Install dotnet for Omnisharp tests
        run: |
          mise use dotnet@8
      - name: Vault
        id: secrets
        uses: SonarSource/vault-action-wrapper@a7fa5fd4a4e4e0f2593f6137c0812cac196cf4ce # 3.7.0
        with:
          secrets: |
            development/kv/data/next url | NEXT_URL;
            development/kv/data/next token | NEXT_TOKEN;
      - name: Cache Sonar Scanner artifacts
        id: sonar-scanner-cache
        uses: SonarSource/ci-github-actions/cache@c3a85ac3a2f67f86966e2fb1fdf9a7c1bdc997dc # 2.2.0
        with:
          path: ~/.sonar/cache
          key: sonar-scanner-${{ runner.os }}
      - uses: SonarSource/ci-github-actions/config-maven@c3a85ac3a2f67f86966e2fb1fdf9a7c1bdc997dc # 2.2.0
        id: config
        with:
          artifactory-reader-role: private-reader
          repox-url: https://repox-internal.dev.sonar.build
      - name: Run tests
        env:
          SONAR_HOST_URL: ${{ fromJSON(steps.secrets.outputs.vault).NEXT_URL }}
          SONAR_TOKEN: ${{ fromJSON(steps.secrets.outputs.vault).NEXT_TOKEN }}
          PROJECT_VERSION: ${{ steps.config.outputs.project-version }}
          SCANNER_VERSION: 5.1.0.4751
          PULL_REQUEST: ${{ github.event.pull_request.number || '' }}
        run: |
          mvn -B -Pcoverage -Dcommercial verify
          maven_goals=("org.sonarsource.scanner.maven:sonar-maven-plugin:${SCANNER_VERSION}:sonar")
          sonar_props=("-Dsonar.host.url=${SONAR_HOST_URL}" "-Dsonar.token=${SONAR_TOKEN}")
          sonar_props+=("-Dsonar.projectVersion=${CURRENT_VERSION}")
          sonar_props+=("-Dsonar.coverage.jacoco.aggregateXmlReportPaths=${{ github.workspace }}/report-aggregate/target/site/jacoco-aggregate/jacoco.xml")
          echo "Maven command: mvn ${maven_goals[*]} ${sonar_props[*]}"
          mvn -B "${maven_goals[@]}" "${sonar_props[@]}"
      - name: Generate test report on failure
        if: failure()
        uses: dorny/test-reporter@a43b3a5f7366b97d083190328d2c652e1a8b6aa2 # v3.0.0
        with:
          name: QA Linux Test Report
          reporter: java-junit
          path: '**/target/surefire-reports/TEST-*.xml,**/target/failsafe-reports/*.xml'
          list-suites: failed
          list-tests: failed
          fail-on-empty: false
      - name: Upload failure diagnostics
        if: failure()
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a # v7.0.1
        with:
          name: linux-test-report
          path: |
            **/target/surefire-reports/**
            **/target/failsafe-reports/**

  test-windows:
    needs: [ build-number, build ]
    runs-on: warp-custom-windows-2022-l
    name: Test (Windows)
    permissions:
      id-token: write
      contents: write
    env:
      BUILD_NUMBER: ${{ needs.build-number.outputs.BUILD_NUMBER }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      - uses: jdx/mise-action@9149ea85001c7435d5a66bb127d6a1b6227cb0a5 # v5.0.0
        with:
          version: 2026.10.21
      - name: Install dotnet for Omnisharp tests
        run: |
          mise use dotnet@8
      - uses: SonarSource/ci-github-actions/config-maven@c3a85ac3a2f67f86966e2fb1fdf9a7c1bdc997dc # 2.2.0
        id: config
        with:
          artifactory-reader-role: private-reader
          repox-url: https://repox-internal.dev.sonar.build
      - name: Run tests
        env:
          MAVEN_OPTS: -Xmx4g
          PROJECT_VERSION: ${{ steps.config.outputs.project-version }}
        run: |
          mvn -B -Dcommercial verify
      - name: Generate test report on failure
        if: failure()
        uses: dorny/test-reporter@a43b3a5f7366b97d083190328d2c652e1a8b6aa2 # v3.0.0
        with:
          name: QA Windows Test Report
          reporter: java-junit
          path: '**/target/surefire-reports/TEST-*.xml,**/target/failsafe-reports/*.xml'
          list-suites: failed
          list-tests: failed
          fail-on-empty: false
      - name: Upload failure diagnostics
        if: failure()
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a # v7.0.1
        with:
          name: windows-test-report
          path: |
            **/target/surefire-reports/**
            **/target/failsafe-reports/**

  qa:
    needs: [ build-number, build ]
    runs-on: sonar-m
    name: QA (${{ matrix.name }})
    permissions:
      id-token: write
      contents: write
    env:
      BUILD_NUMBER: ${{ needs.build-number.outputs.BUILD_NUMBER }}
    strategy:
      fail-fast: true
      matrix:
        include:
          - name: SonarCloudEU
            sq_version: SonarCloudEU
            category: "-Dgroups=SonarCloud"
            sc: true
            sc_token_path: sonarcloud-it
            region: EU
          - name: SonarCloudUS
            sq_version: SonarCloudUS
            category: "-Dgroups=SonarCloud"
            sc: true
            sc_token_path: sonarcloud-it-US
            region: US
          - name: SQDogfood
            sq_version: DEV
            # Run the latest CLI compatibility test once in normal QA.
            category: "-DexcludedGroups=SonarCloud"
          - name: SQLatest
            sq_version: LATEST_RELEASE
            category: "-DexcludedGroups=SonarCloud,CliCompatibility"
          - name: SQLts251
            sq_version: "LATEST_RELEASE[2025.1]"
            category: "-DexcludedGroups=SonarCloud,CliCompatibility -Dsurefire.failIfNoSpecifiedTests=false -Dtest=SonarQubeDeveloperEditionTests,SonarQubeEnterpriseEditionTests"
          - name: SQcb251
            sq_version: "LATEST_RELEASE[25.1]"
            category: "-DexcludedGroups=SonarCloud,CliCompatibility -Dsurefire.failIfNoSpecifiedTests=false -Dtest=FileExclusionTests,SonarQubeCommunityEditionTests"
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      - uses: jdx/mise-action@9149ea85001c7435d5a66bb127d6a1b6227cb0a5 # v5.0.0
        with:
          version: 2026.10.21
      - name: Setup Java ${{ matrix.customOrchestratorJavaVersion }} for Orchestrator
        if: matrix.customOrchestratorJavaVersion
        run: |
          mise install java@${{ matrix.customOrchestratorJavaVersion }}
          echo "ORCHESTRATOR_JAVA_HOME=$(mise where java@${{ matrix.customOrchestratorJavaVersion }})" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
      - name: Compute month key
        #Avoid caching for DEV since it is frequently changing
        if: ${{ matrix.sc != true && matrix.sq_version != 'DEV' }}
        id: month
        shell: bash
        run: |
          THIS_MONTH="$(date +%Y-%m)"
          echo "month=${THIS_MONTH}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          ORCHESTRATOR_HOME="${GITHUB_WORKSPACE}/orchestrator/${THIS_MONTH}"
          echo "ORCHESTRATOR_HOME=${ORCHESTRATOR_HOME}" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
          echo "Create dir ${ORCHESTRATOR_HOME} if needed"
          mkdir -p "${ORCHESTRATOR_HOME}"
      - uses: SonarSource/ci-github-actions/cache@c3a85ac3a2f67f86966e2fb1fdf9a7c1bdc997dc # 2.2.0
        if: ${{ github.event_name != 'pull_request' && matrix.sc != true && matrix.sq_version != 'DEV' }}
        with:
          path: ${{ github.workspace }}/orchestrator/${{ steps.month.outputs.month }}
          key: cache-production-${{ runner.os }}-${{ steps.month.outputs.month }}-${{ matrix.name }} # Use matrix name to differentiate caches
      - name: Vault (SonarCloud IT token)
        if: ${{ matrix.sc == true }}
        id: secrets-sc
        uses: SonarSource/vault-action-wrapper@a7fa5fd4a4e4e0f2593f6137c0812cac196cf4ce # 3.7.0
        with:
          secrets: |
            development/team/sonarlint/kv/data/${{ matrix.sc_token_path }} token | SONARCLOUD_IT_TOKEN;
      - name: Vault (GITHUB Token)
        id: secrets-gh
        uses: SonarSource/vault-action-wrapper@a7fa5fd4a4e4e0f2593f6137c0812cac196cf4ce # 3.7.0
        with:
          secrets: |
            development/github/token/licenses-ro token | GITHUB_TOKEN;
            development/artifactory-edge-prod/token/{REPO_OWNER_NAME_DASH}-private-reader access_token | ORCHESTRATOR_ACCESS_TOKEN;
      - name: Configure production Orchestrator
        shell: bash
        env:
          ORCHESTRATOR_ACCESS_TOKEN: ${{ fromJSON(steps.secrets-gh.outputs.vault).ORCHESTRATOR_ACCESS_TOKEN }}
        run: |
          umask 077
          config_dir="$RUNNER_TEMP/orchestrator-production-config"
          mkdir -p "$config_dir"
          printf '%s\n' \
            'orchestrator.artifactory.url=https://repox-internal.sonar.build/artifactory' \
            "orchestrator.artifactory.accessToken=$ORCHESTRATOR_ACCESS_TOKEN" > "$config_dir/orchestrator.properties"
          config_path="$config_dir/orchestrator.properties"
          if [[ "$RUNNER_OS" == Windows ]]; then
            config_path="/$(cygpath -m "$config_path")"
          fi
          config_path="${config_path// /%20}"
          echo "ORCHESTRATOR_CONFIG_URL=file://$config_path" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"

      - uses: SonarSource/ci-github-actions/config-maven@c3a85ac3a2f67f86966e2fb1fdf9a7c1bdc997dc # 2.2.0
        with:
          artifactory-reader-role: private-reader
          repox-url: https://repox-internal.dev.sonar.build
      - name: Run QA
        if: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' || github.ref_name == github.event.repository.default_branch || startsWith(github.ref_name, 'branch-') || startsWith(github.ref_name, 'dogfood-on-') }}
        env:
          MAVEN_OPTS: -Xmx4g
          SONARCLOUD_IT_TOKEN: ${{ steps.secrets-sc.outputs.vault && fromJSON(steps.secrets-sc.outputs.vault).SONARCLOUD_IT_TOKEN || '' }}
          SONARCLOUD_REGION: ${{ matrix.sc && matrix.region || '' }}
          GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ fromJSON(steps.secrets-gh.outputs.vault).GITHUB_TOKEN }}
          ORCHESTRATOR_HOME: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' && format('{0}/orchestrator-production', runner.temp) || env.ORCHESTRATOR_HOME || format('{0}/orchestrator-production', runner.temp) }}
          SONAR_SEARCH_JAVAADDITIONALOPTS: -XX:-UseContainerSupport
          SONAR_WEB_JAVAADDITIONALOPTS: -XX:-UseContainerSupport
          SONAR_CE_JAVAADDITIONALOPTS: -XX:-UseContainerSupport
        run: |
          mvn "-Dorchestrator.configUrl=$ORCHESTRATOR_CONFIG_URL" "-Dorchestrator.home=$ORCHESTRATOR_HOME" -f its/pom.xml -Dsonar.runtimeVersion=${{ matrix.sq_version }} ${{ matrix.category }} verify surefire-report:report
      - name: Generate QA test report on failure
        if: failure()
        uses: dorny/test-reporter@2dcf091ad558da2cabf16f6b423e02cd078c937a
        with:
          name: QA ${{ matrix.name }} Test Report
          reporter: java-junit
          path: '**/target/surefire-reports/TEST-*.xml,**/target/failsafe-reports/*.xml'
          list-suites: failed
          list-tests: failed
          fail-on-empty: false
      - name: Upload failure diagnostics
        if: failure()
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a # v7.0.1
        with:
          name: qa-test-report ${{ matrix.name }}
          path: |
            **/target/surefire-reports/**
            **/target/failsafe-reports/**
      - name: debug
        if: failure()
        shell: bash
        run: |
          echo "=== Listing surefire-reports contents ==="
          find ./its/tests/target/surefire-reports -type f || true
          echo "=== Checking if directory is empty ==="
          [ -d ./its/tests/target/surefire-reports ] && ls -la ./its/tests/target/surefire-reports/ || echo "Directory doesn't exist"
      - name: Inspect Orchestrator Cache
        if: always()
        shell: bash
        run: |
          echo "=== Listing orchestrator cache contents ==="
          CACHE_DIR="${{ github.workspace }}/orchestrator/${{ steps.month.outputs.month }}"
          if [ -d "${CACHE_DIR}" ]; then
            echo "Directory exists: ${CACHE_DIR}"
            ls -lah "${CACHE_DIR}"
            echo ""
            echo "=== Detailed file tree ==="
            find "${CACHE_DIR}" -type f -ls || true
          else
            echo "Directory does not exist: ${CACHE_DIR}"
          fi

  promote:
    needs: [ build-number, build, qa, test-linux, test-windows ]
    runs-on: sonar-xs
    name: Promote
    permissions:
      id-token: write
      contents: write
    env:
      BUILD_NUMBER: ${{ needs.build-number.outputs.BUILD_NUMBER }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      - uses: SonarSource/ci-github-actions/promote@c3a85ac3a2f67f86966e2fb1fdf9a7c1bdc997dc # 2.2.0
        with:
          promote-pull-request: true",
  "rationale": "The qa job runs a six-cell matrix with fail-fast: false, so every cell runs even after one fails. Since promote depends on qa passing, any single cell failure already fails qa and blocks promote; remaining cells cannot change the pass/fail outcome. Setting fail-fast: true cancels remaining matrix cells on the first failure, saving CI resources while preserving all test coverage for passing cells and retaining failure diagnostics from cells that completed. This matches the P-LIT-FAIL-FAST pattern (cancel remaining matrix jobs after failure), supported by experiment records batch-scenario-three-run-4bb0552aeb09c242 and batch-scenario-three-run-b6e04fef7ef24997 (both scenario_passed). No permissions, secrets, deployment, or network changes are introduced.",
  "evidence_ids": ["experiment:batch-scenario-three-run-4bb0552aeb09c242", "experiment:batch-scenario-three-run-b6e04fef7ef24997"]
}
message.reasoning:
The user wants me to propose a CI optimization for the given workflow based on evidence. Let me analyze the workflow and the evidence.

The workflow is a Maven-based Java project (SonarLint) with:
- `build-number` job (sonar-xs)
- `build` job (sonar-xs) - builds with Maven, skips tests
- `test-linux` job (sonar-m) - needs build-number, build
- `test-windows` job (warp-custom-windows-2022-l) - needs build-number, build
- `qa` job (sonar-m) - matrix with multiple QA configurations, needs build-number, build
- `promote` job (sonar-xs) - needs build-number, build, qa, test-linux, test-windows

The concurrency section cancels in-progress runs.

Evidence patterns available:
- P-LIT-FAIL-FAST: Cancel remaining matrix jobs after failure. The `qa` job has `fail-fast: false`. Setting it to `true` would cancel remaining matrix jobs if one fails. But the contraindication says "Every matrix outcome is required" - we need to check if all QA matrix results are required. The `promote` job needs `qa`, so if qa fails, promote won't run. But individual matrix cells... if one QA cell fails, the qa job fails. With fail-fast: false, all cells run. With fail-fast: true, remaining cells cancel on failure. This could save resources. But the evidence is synthetic and the limitation says "Source branch-protection and required-check safety need a separate applicability review." Also "Every matrix outcome is required" is a contraindication. Since promote depends on qa, and qa is likely a required check, we might not want to cancel remaining matrix jobs because we might want full diagnostics. However, if one cell fails, the job fails anyway, so running more cells doesn't change the outcome. But for diagnostics, you might want all results. This is a judgment call.

- P-LIT-CUSTOM-TIMEOUT: Bound jobs with custom timeout. The workflow has no `timeout-minutes` on any job. Adding timeouts could prevent runaway consumption. But we don't have representative successful-duration history to set appropriate timeouts. The evidence says preconditions: "Representative successful-duration history exists." We have CI history showing runs but no durations. So this might not be supported.

- P-LIT-GHA-CACHE: Cache dependency downloads. The workflow uses Maven. There's a step "Config Maven (cache setup)" that runs `mvn -B -e -V -Pits dependency:go-offline` to populate cache. But there's no explicit cache action around it. However, the `mise-action` has `cache: npm` but that's for Node. For Maven, there's no cache action. Adding a Maven dependency cache could help. But the evidence is observational with modest benefit. The contraindications: "Mutable or untrusted cached content", "An equivalent cache already exists". The `dependency:go-offline` step populates the local Maven repo, but without a cache action, it's lost between runs. Adding `actions/cache` for the local Maven repository (~/.m2/repository) keyed on lockfiles (pom.xml) could be beneficial. But we need to be careful not to weaken permissions or add network access - cache is fine.

- P-LIT-CANCEL-STALE: Cancel superseded runs. The workflow already has `concurrency: cancel-in-progress: true`. This cancels in-progress runs on the same concurrency group. The concurrency group is based on workflow + branch/PR. This already handles canceling superseded runs for the same branch/PR. So this is already implemented.

- P-LIT-FAIL-FAST: The `qa` job has `fail-fast: false`. Looking at the evidence, the experiment examples show changing `fail-fast: false` to `fail-fast: true` in a matrix. The pattern P-LIT-FAIL-FAST is about canceling remaining matrix jobs after failure. The `qa` job is a matrix job. If one QA configuration fails, do we need the others? The `promote` job depends on `qa` completing successfully. If any QA cell fails, `qa` fails and `promote` won't run. So canceling remaining cells on failure would save resources without changing the outcome (promote won't run anyway). However, for diagnostic purposes, you might want all results. But the evidence supports this as an optimization.

Wait, let me re-read the evidence more carefully. The evidence records are "experiment_example" with synthetic workloads. The pattern P-LIT-FAIL-FAST has:
- preconditions: ["Matrix failure makes remaining results dispensable under an explicit study policy"]
- contraindications: ["Every matrix outcome is required", "Full failure diagnostics are required"]

The `qa` job matrix has 6 configurations. Are all outcomes required? The `promote` job needs `qa` to pass. If any cell fails, `qa` fails. So remaining results are dispensable in terms of the pass/fail outcome. But for diagnostics, you might want to know which configurations fail. However, the test report on failure step would capture failures from the cells that did run.

Actually, looking at the evidence IDs, I need to use "supported evidence IDs". The evidence provided in the prompt includes several experiment examples. Let me identify which ones are relevant and have outcome "scenario_passed" or similar.

The evidence records with document_ids:
1. experiment:batch-scenario-three-run-4bb0552aeb09c242 - P-LIT-FAIL-FAST, outcome: scenario_passed
2. experiment:batch-scenario-three-run-b6e04fef7ef24997 - P-LIT-FAIL-FAST, outcome: scenario_passed
3. experiment:batch-scenario-three-run-616492d40289f26f-r5 - P-LIT-ENV-CACHE, outcome: scenario_passed
4. experiment:batch-scenario-three-run-5d1aa22691509a8e-r5 - P-LIT-ENV-CACHE, outcome: scenario_passed
5. experiment:batch-interactive-three--fb8b16eb65a11508 - P-LIT-CUSTOM-TIMEOUT, outcome: null

And the pattern catalogue entries have document_ids like "pattern:P-LIT-GHA-CACHE", etc.

The instruction says "Use only supported evidence IDs; APPLY requires at least one."

I think the most applicable optimization here is P-LIT-FAIL-FAST for the `qa` job matrix. The `qa` job has `fail-fast: false` and a matrix of 6 configurations. Setting `fail-fast: true` would cancel remaining matrix jobs when one fails, saving CI resources. The `promote` job depends on `qa`, so if any QA cell fails, promote won't run regardless. This preserves build and test coverage (all cells still run unless one fails, in which case the job is already failing).

But wait - is there a contraindication? "Every matrix outcome is required" - if the repository requires all QA matrix results to be collected (e.g., for compliance or comprehensive diagnostics), then fail-fast would be inappropriate. But the workflow doesn't indicate that. The `promote` job just needs `qa` to pass.

Actually, let me reconsider. The evidence for P-LIT-FAIL-FAST is synthetic and the limitations say "Source branch-protection and required-check safety need a separate applicability review." The required_checks status is "not_verified". So we can't be sure if all matrix outcomes are required.

Hmm, but the task says to propose an optimization that fits. Let me think about what's most clearly supported.

Another option: P-LIT-CUSTOM-TIMEOUT. The workflow has no timeouts on any job. Adding `timeout-minutes` could prevent runaway consumption. But we don't have duration history to set appropriate values. The evidence says preconditions: "Representative successful-duration history exists." We have CI history but no durations. So we can't set a meaningful timeout.

P-LIT-GHA-CACHE: The workflow builds with Maven and has a `dependency:go-offline` step but no cache action. Adding a cache for ~/.m2/repository could help. But the evidence is observational with modest benefit, and we'd need to check if lockfiles are used for cache keys. Maven uses pom.xml. This seems applicable.

Actually, looking more carefully at the workflow, the `build` job runs `mvn -B -e -V -Pits dependency:go-offline` to populate cache, but there's no `actions/cache` step to save/restore it. This means every run re-downloads dependencies. Adding a cache action around the Maven local repository would be a clear optimization.

But wait - the `build` job is the one that builds, and `test-linux`, `test-windows`, `qa` all need the build output. They each checkout and run Maven again. The `dependency:go-offline` is only in the `build` job. The test jobs run `mvn verify` which would need dependencies. Without a cache, they re-download.

Actually, looking at the `build` job:
```
- name: Config Maven (cache setup)
  run: |
    mvn -B -e -V -Pits dependency:go-offline # populate cache including ITs deps too
```
This populates the local Maven repo but doesn't cache it. So subsequent jobs (test-linux, test-windows, qa) would need to re-download or the build job's local repo isn't shared (different runners).

Adding `actions/cache` for ~/.m2/repository in each job (or at least the test jobs) keyed on pom.xml files could save time. But this is a significant change and might require careful key design.

Let me reconsider P-LIT-FAIL-FAST. The `qa` job has:
```yaml
strategy:
  fail-fast: false
  matrix:
    include:
      - name: SonarCloudEU
        ...
```
